[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Atomic proc schema and lifecycle[/bold #D7AFFF]                              [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]proc-store-lifecycle[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]proc-store-lifecycle: extend the Rust proc wire and Python parity models[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]with additive/defaulted proc-shell, ownership, timeout, result, stop, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]and settlement fields; split permissive legacy reads from strict [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]new-write validation; and replace generic append/update ownership with [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]locked reserve, stop-request, supervisor-claim, and single-owner finish [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]operations. Enforce immutable non-empty argv, active shell-name and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]concurrency-key conflicts, idempotent fingerprint replay, explicit [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]supported schema versions, and settling-before-terminal invariants while[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]keeping legacy command/tui/detached and commandless TUI rows readable. [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]Add Rust, PyO3/wire-parity, and Python facade tests for concurrent [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]reservations, invalid transitions, replay, legacy parsing, and retention[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]ownership boundaries.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]One detached proc service and supervisor[/bold #D7AFFF]                      [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]unified-proc-supervisor[dim] · [dim][/dim]after proc-store-lifecycle[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]unified-proc-supervisor: introduce one typed Python proc submission [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]request and service over the new Rust lifecycle, then promote the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]monitor bootstrap/supervision guarantees into the proc kernel: [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]double-fork/reparenting, bounded acknowledgement and launch barrier, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]scrubbed child environment, boot-aware supervisor identity, direct [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]persisted argv execution, merged binary-safe output, total and idle [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]timeouts, process-group TERM-to-KILL escalation, stop intent, and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]reboot/pid-reuse/loss reconciliation. Move through settling and make [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]settlement resumable and idempotent so the command, output, result [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]envelope, workspace claim, artifacts, and follow-up policy are durable [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]before terminal state. Keep Proc.log_path authoritative and only prune [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]store-owned logs below the proc log root. Migrate ordinary proc CLI/API [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]callers to the service, retaining compatibility reconciliation for [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]already-running legacy rows and removing the weaker supervisor only [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]after focused crash-boundary tests pass.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Named proc-shell addressing and CLI[/bold #D7AFFF]                           [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]named-proc-shell-cli[dim] · [dim][/dim]after unified-proc-supervisor[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]named-proc-shell-cli: add -N/--shell to proc run and list, resolve [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]show/kill references by exact fully qualified shell name before exact id[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]and unique id prefix, and derive bare names beneath the calling sase [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]agent. Validate names against slash, proc-id ambiguity, invalid agent [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]components, and malformed qualification; map each shell name to its [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]distinct namespaced concurrency key without conflating the fields; scope[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]active uniqueness by project and allow reuse only after settlement. [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]Update filtering, JSON and rich renderers, help, completions, and tests [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]using “named proc shell” language while preserving historical name [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]visibility and avoiding a top-level sase shell command.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Family-attached monitor facade and settlement[/bold #D7AFFF]                 [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]monitor-proc-facade[dim] · [dim][/dim]after unified-proc-supervisor, [/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#AF87FF][dim]named-proc-shell-cli[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]monitor-proc-facade: reimplement monitor start/list/show/stop as direct [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]calls and projections over the shared proc service so one monitor has [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]one proc id and no duplicate execution state or wrapper process. Compile[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the monitor command remainder to explicit \[/bin/sh, -c, command] argv, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]attach a shell_kind=proc artifacts member to the target sase agent, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]preserve family allocation, status labels, workspace-claim transfer, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]bounded output, total/idle timeout, stop, and exactly-once --next [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]behavior, and store immutable proc/artifacts cross-links. Correct [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]required-option CLI-rule violations by using a command positional and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]optional policy defaults, retain hidden compatibility aliases/readers [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]for historical monitor records, and never adopt a live legacy monitor. [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]Cover starter death, launch failures, quiet and invalid-UTF8 output, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]background grandchildren, resistant process groups, claim [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]transfer/release, and follow-up replay/suppression.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  5 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Service cutover and compatibility verification[/bold #D7AFFF]                [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]proc-platform-cutover[dim] · [dim][/dim]after monitor-proc-facade[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]proc-platform-cutover: collapse bead task/epic launch monitoring onto [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the shared service and audit all remaining proc/monitor writers so new [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]records use the unified lifecycle while legacy readers and control paths[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]remain intact. Verify consistent ids, state, logs, names, and family [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]projections across proc CLI, monitor CLI, agent listings, and current [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]ACE observation without migrating ACE-owned producer APIs reserved for [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the following parent phase. Exercise concurrent processes, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]replay/conflict diagnostics, crash recovery at every settlement [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]boundary, reboot and pid reuse, retention of artifacts-owned logs, and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]old store fixtures. Update the generated monitor skill source and user [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]documentation, run just install and focused suites throughout, then run [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]just check-full via sase monitor with a follow-up action; run visual [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]tests only if existing ACE rendering changes.[/#D7D7AF]
